answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer: No. Do not add Thursday's 5 miles or the 2 miles short on Sunday. A tired body absorbs extra miles poorly, and the risk of a setback outweighs any gain. The 30 miles next week rebuild the base from here, and the missed miles stay missed.

new.analysis:
## What changed last week

The week came in at 27 miles against 36 planned, and three sessions changed. Wednesday's threshold stopped at 6 miles after two of three reps, Thursday's 5-mile easy run did not happen, and Sunday's long run ended at 11 of 13 miles.

Heat was the main driver. The air was already 27 degrees at 6am, the apartment AC was out, and you stopped twice for water on the long run. Stopping the threshold work was the right call, because heart rate was far above where it should be for that pace.

| Measure | Aug 17 – 23 | Aug 24 – 30 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy-run average heart rate | 138 bpm | 151 bpm |
| Long run | 10 mi at 10:02/mi, 146 bpm | 11 mi at 11:14/mi, 156 bpm |

The long-run pace includes your stops for water. The rise in heart rate reflects heat and fatigue rather than lost fitness. Easy time in zones 1 and 2 fell to about 11 percent because the heat pushed easy runs into zone 3. Sleep at 5.5 hours and feeling drained point the same way, so this week is as much about recovery as training.

## The week ahead

Next week totals 30 miles, a modest step up from the 27 you ran last week. That keeps the build moving without stacking fatigue on a body that is still absorbing the last two weeks. The AC is due back next week, which should help sleep.

Wednesday stays the only quality session, shortened to two reps. Run it by effort and heart rate rather than pace. In heat the pace will likely be slower than 8:00 per mile, and that is acceptable. The aim is to finish with a third rep still in reserve.

The long run stays easy at 11 miles, and marathon-pace work waits. Adding it now would load a tired body that is not yet absorbing the work. It can return in two to three weeks, once sleep and heat settle.

## Where this leaves the race

Finishing under 3:45 needs about 8:35 per mile on race day. Your long run is about two hours at easy effort right now. It needs to reach 2.5 to 3 hours before Nov 1, so it should grow in steady steps. Catching up on missed miles would work against that goal.

safetyCallouts.title: Lingering tiredness.
safetyCallouts.body: Feeling tired all the time on about 5.5 hours of sleep is worth a check with your doctor. If you still feel drained after this lighter week, see a doctor before adding any load.

safetyCallouts.title: Right knee flare.
safetyCallouts.body: If the knee hurts again, especially sharp pain on downhills, stop running for the day and see a physio before the next long run.
